metaTitle: OpenCartable — compose a course, share it by link
metaDescription: A free, self-hosted teaching platform: compose your courses, illustrate them with formulas and interactive modules, and share them with your students through a link, no account needed.

hero.title: Compose your courses, share them by link
hero.lead: OpenCartable brings together course writing, interactive modules and AI support — then puts all of it in your students' hands through a single link. They have no account to create.
hero.license: Free software under the AGPL v3 licence, built to be hosted on your own machine.

compose.title: Compose and organise your courses
compose.lead: Write, illustrate, file away. The course comes together in the order you teach it, and everything is saved as you type.

editor.title: A course that follows your teaching
editor.body: Put the course together in the order you teach it, and rearrange it when your plan changes.

resources.title: Your documents with the course
resources.body: PDFs, images, audio and video live in the course library and drop in wherever you want on the page. They travel with the course when you share it.

classify.title: Filed by subject and level
classify.body: Every course finds its place in the taxonomy: you find your way around, and your students find you.

compose.note: An example course is waiting from your very first sign-in, so you never start from a blank page.

content.title: Illustrate your course effortlessly
content.lead: Formulas, diagrams and figures are written as text and draw themselves. Nothing to install, nothing to export as an image.

math.title: Maths that stay maths
math.body: Your LaTeX formulas are typeset on screen and stay crisp in print, never flattened into a screenshot.

diagrams.title: Diagrams described in one line
diagrams.body: A flowchart or a sequence diagram is described as text, and draws itself.

geometry.title: Figures students can handle
geometry.body: GeoGebra constructions, JSXGraph figures, TikZ drawings: geometry becomes something to play with mid-course.

docs.title: Help within reach
docs.body: Every syntax has its documentation page inside the application, with examples you edit live.

modules.title: Drop a web module into the course
modules.lead: A simulation, a drill, an animation: write it in HTML, CSS and JavaScript without leaving the application, and place it between two paragraphs.

editors.title: Written and seen on the spot
editors.body: Three editors and a live preview: the module comes to life while you write it.

sandbox.title: Run with no risk
sandbox.body: The module runs locked in, with no access to your data and none to the network: all it can do is display.

reuse.title: Reusable across the course
reuse.body: Every module joins the course library and drops in wherever you want, as many times as you need.

share.title: Share by link, with no student account
share.lead: Your students open the link and get to work. No sign-up, no password, no list to keep at the start of the year.

noAccount.title: Nothing to create, nothing to delete
noAccount.body: The link carries the access: no identity to administer, in September or in June.

control.title: You stay in control
control.body: A link can be revoked and expires on its own, and every course stays draft, private or public as you choose.

reading.title: A reading view made for them
reading.body: Contents, resources, modules, full course: your students work through it block by block without getting lost.

exercises.title: Exercises done online
exercises.body: They write their answers in the browser; the model answers, meanwhile, never leave the server.

share.note: Sharing happens at course level: opening a course opens access to its whole library, and there is no file-by-file sharing.

search.title: Or let them find you
search.body: Public search is open to everyone without an account, by subject and by level. You only appear in the directory if you ask to be there.

ai.title: An assistant that writes with you
ai.lead: The assistant reads the course you are writing, answers your questions and proposes rewrites. You are the one who decides, every time.
ai.principle: The AI proposes, you decide: no change is applied without your approval.

context.title: It knows your course
context.body: It reads your blocks, your PDFs, your images and your modules, and cites the passage each answer comes from.

rewrite.title: It rewrites what you show it
rewrite.body: A paragraph to clarify, an exercise question to reword, a module to fix: the proposal arrives ready to review.

undo.title: Nothing irreversible
undo.body: An accepted proposal is undone like any keystroke, with a Ctrl-Z.

cost.title: The cost in plain sight
cost.body: Every exchange shows what it consumed: no surprise at the end of the month.

ai.limit: The assistant does not replace your own proofreading, and it never edits a course on its own.

tutor.title: A tutor that marks your students
tutor.lead: A signed-in student submits an answer and gets immediate feedback, question by question — with nothing for you to collect.

feedback.title: Immediate feedback
feedback.body: The tutor assesses the answer, says what works and what is missing, and sends the student back in without handing over the solution.

thread.title: One thread per question
thread.body: Every question keeps its own conversation: the student picks up where they left off, as many times as needed.

reveal.title: The answer at the right moment
reveal.body: The server decides when the model answer may be revealed — not the model, and not the student.

tutor.limit: The tutor supports the student: it produces no marks and no report cards.

sovereignty.title: Your key, your model
sovereignty.lead: OpenCartable imposes no AI provider — not even its own. You plug in yours, you switch, or you do without.

providers.mistral: Mistral, hosted in the European Union

local.title: Nothing leaves your machine
local.body: With a model served by Ollama on your own machine, no course text ever goes to a third party.

switch.title: Several models, one click
switch.body: Keep one model for drafting and another for proofreading, and switch from the foot of the chat.

encryption.title: Your keys kept safe
encryption.body: They are stored encrypted and are never shown back to you.

default.title: Or nothing to set up
default.body: Without a key, the instance's default AI stays available, within a daily quota.

selfHost.title: Host it yourself, keep your courses
selfHost.lead: OpenCartable installs with Docker Compose, right down to a Raspberry Pi. Your courses stay yours — and you can leave with them.

docker.title: One command to start
docker.body: Docker Compose brings up the application, the API and the database, on ARM64 as well as x86-64.

export.title: Your courses leave with you
export.body: A course exports to an archive and imports back, unchanged, into another instance.

pdf.title: A clean PDF in one print
pdf.body: Vector formulas and selectable text: the course prints without going through a converter.

privacy.title: No third party in the loop
privacy.body: No password kept, no font loaded from outside, no third-party service between your students and your courses.

a11y.title: Built for everyone
a11y.body: Bilingual interface, light and dark themes, contrast and keyboard navigation checked.

license.title: Free, under the AGPL v3
license.body: The code is published, and any instance put online must make its changes available.

scope.title: What OpenCartable is not
scope.lead: A clear boundary beats a vague promise.

notItems.grades: No marks, no report cards, no averages.
notItems.messaging: No messaging between teachers, students or families.
notItems.classroom: No classroom management, no attendance, no timetable.

scope.is: OpenCartable is a place where your courses are composed, kept alive and shared. The rest, your school's own information system already does.

final.title: Start with one course
final.lead: Sign in: an example course is waiting to get you going in a few minutes.
final.source: View the source code on GitHub
